caseno: Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 463 of 2009
lawyer:
Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan, Senior Advocate Instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Respondent Nos ----- Not represented
parties:
Puron Gonju ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Abdul Haque and others ----- Respondents
case_source: (From the Judgment and order dated 1.12.2008 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 7 of 2007)
full_judgment:
B. K. Das J.:- This Petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 1st December, 2008 of a learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in making the rule issued in Civil Revision No. 07 of 2007 absolute. 

2. The petitioner No. 1 herein as plaintiff instituted a suit being Title Suit No. 74 of 1994 for declaration of title and for further declaration that registered kabala being No.6996 dated 02.07.1991 executed by tile defendant nos. 1 and 2 in favour of defendant No. 3 was collusive, void and not binding upon the plaintiff' and also for recovery of khas possession by evicting the defendants therefrom. The suit was decreed on compromise with defendant No. 1 and 2 and ex-pare against the rest by judgment and decree dated 02.09.2002. Then, the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 made an application under order IX Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure being Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2006 for restoration of the suit to its original file and number after set-ting aside the experte decree. 

3. The plaintiff, meanwhile, put the decree in execution being Title Execution Case No. 2 of 2006. The defendant Nos. 4 to 6 on 1.3.09.2006 made as application for stay of further proceedings of the execution case till disposal of the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case. By an order dated 08.10.2006 the Executing Court rejected the application on the view that as there was no suit pending, such application was not maintainable. 

4. Being aggrieved, the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 made an application under section 115(2) of the Code of Civil procedure for revision of such order of the Executing Court but by an order dated 8.10.2006 revision application was rejected in affirming the order of the Executing Court. 

5. Being aggrieved thereby the respondent as petitioner moved the High Court Division in revision being Civil Revision No. 7 of 2007 and a learned Single Judge upon hearing the parties by judgment and order dated 1st December, 2008 made the rule absolute and further proceedings of the execution case in question was stayed till disposal of Miscellaneous case No. 23 of 2006. 

6. The decree-holder-petitioner being dissatisfied with the said order of the High Court Division filed the instant petition. 

7. We have heard the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner Mr. Abdul Wadud Bhuiyan and considered the impugned judgment and all other materials on record Mr. Bhuiyan for the petitioner submits that the revisional court found that the plaintiff-petitioner having got the decree On compromise on 2.9.2002 (decree singed on 9.9.2009 is legally entitled to get the benefit thereof and that the Miscellaneous Case No. 23 of 2006 was filed by defendant Nos. 4 to 6, after about three and half years under Order 9 Rule 13 and that the learned Senior Assistant Judge, upon overall consideration rejected the application for stay of further proceedings of the execution case and the lower appellate court affirmed the same upon finding also that it was not at all proper to stay further proceedings of the execution case after such a long time on the plea of non service of summons raised by the defendant Nos. 4 to 6 and the High Court Division without adverting to the reasons given by the lower appellate court reversed the concurrent decision and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. The learned Advocate for the petitioner further submits that the lower appellate court having affirmed the decision of the learned Senior Assistant Judge given on the application under order 21 Rule 29 read with section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure by giving cogent reasons, the High Court Division committed an error of law in reversing the concurrent decision and therefore, the judgment of the High Court Division is not sustainable in law. 

8. We find merit in the submissions of the learned Senior Advocate for the petitioner. Leave is accordingly granted. 

9. The petitioner is directed to deposit security of Taka.1,000/- within 1 (one) month. 

10. The petitioner is permitted to prepare the paper book out of court in accordance with rules. 

End.
